memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, "Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?" The midwives answered Pharaoh, "Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women; they are vigorous and give birth before the midwives arrive."" - Exodus 1:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh calls them in and demands an explanation. Imagine standing there — two ordinary women, before a throne, answering for disobedience that could cost them their lives.

Their answer has puzzled readers for centuries. Was it entirely true? Scripture does not tell us; it neither praises their words nor condemns them. What the text plainly commends is their fear of God and their refusal to kill children. We should be careful not to build a doctrine about deception out of a verse that simply does not address it. Honest readers across the church have differed here, and the passage itself keeps its focus elsewhere.

What is unmistakable is this: these women valued life more than their own safety, and they did not crumble when questioned.

Most of us will not face a Pharaoh. But we will face moments where standing for what is right becomes uncomfortable and we are asked, why did you do that? In such moments Jesus promised His followers help — the Spirit giving them what to say when they are dragged before authorities (Lk 12:11-12).

Do the right thing first. God will handle the summons.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I make decisions based on what is right, or on what is safest?
2. Am I quick to judge others where Scripture itself is silent?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me courage to protect what is right even when I must answer for it. Steady my heart and guard my words. Amen.
